data.name: Lingaraj
data.gender_notes: Lingaraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lingaraj is a name derived from two Sanskrit words: Linga and Raja. Linga symbolizes the phallic form of Lord Shiva, while Raja means king. Thus, Lingaraj refers to the divine king, a manifestation of Lord Shiva. The name Lingaraj carries the meaning “Linga (symbol of Shiva) + Raja (king)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lingaraj usually hope their child will grow to embody linga (symbol of shiva) + raja (king) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine kingship and spiritual enlightenment.
data.etymology: Lingaraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Linga (symbol of Shiva) + Raja (king).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lingaraj total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Lingaraj is a significant name in the Hindu culture, representing the worship of Lord Shiva in his phallic form called Lingam. The Lingam is considered a symbol of creation and represents the divine masculine energy. The name signifies the reverence and devotion towards Shiva, who is believed to be the cause of all creation and destruction. Worship of Lingaraj is popular across India, with several temples dedicated to this deity, including the famous Lingaraj Temple in Odisha.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Lingaraj symbolizes the unity of the masculine (Shiva) and feminine (Shakti) energies in the universe. The phallic symbol of Shiva, as Lingam, represents the creative force – the beginning, sustenance, and end of all existence. Through reverence and devotion to Lingaraj, devotees seek salvation, purification of their souls, and attainment of spiritual knowledge. This is because, as per Hindu scriptures, recognizing and connecting with the divine presence in its feminine aspect (Shakti) and masculine aspect (Shiva) leads to enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lingaraj signifies the divine phallic symbol of Lord Shiva, embodying the creative and destructive aspects of the universe. It is a reminder of the cyclic nature of existence and the interplay of male and female energies.

historical_references.reference: Lingaraj Temple, Bhubaneswar is one of the oldest temples in India, believed to have been built in the 11th century during the Eastern Ganga Dynasty. It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is known for its intricate carvings and sculptures.
historical_references.context: Eastern Ganga Dynasty, Bhubaneswar, Lord Shiva temple, intricate carvings and sculptures

historical_references.reference: Lingaraj Temple is also known as 'Temple of Trimurti', as it is the only temple in India where all three Gods - Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh (Shiva) are present in their respective forms.
historical_references.context: Hinduism, Trimurti, presence of all three Gods - Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva in their respective forms

In modern times, Lingaraj is a popular figure in Hindu spirituality, tourism, and social media platforms. On Instagram, devotees and spiritual enthusiasts often post images and stories of Lingaraj temples and idols, using hashtags like #Lingaraj, #Shiva, and #Hinduism. On Facebook, various temple committees and spiritual organizations create pages dedicated to Lingaraj, where they share information about rituals, festivals, and other cultural events. In addition, Reddit communities like r/Hinduism and r/Shiva have discussions and share content related to Lingaraj and other aspects of Hinduism. The global trend towards increased spiritual awareness and the desire to connect with one's cultural heritage has led to a growing interest in Lingaraj and other Hindu deities on social media platforms.
